title: The normalization is the coproduct of the normalizations of the reduced irreducible components

standard_prerequisites.name: The normalization is unchanged by passing to the reduction of the base, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the base to be assumed reduced.

standard_prerequisites.name: The local description of the normalization by integral closures, and the structural statement that the normalization is universal for factorizations through locally birational integral morphisms, both cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Give two alternative routes to identify the coproduct as the normalization.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a reduced scheme with locally finitely many irreducible components the coproduct of the components is integral and locally birational over the base
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the hypothesis under which the structural statement applies.

core_obligations: Reduce to the reduced case: the normalization does not change when the base is replaced by its reduction, so one may assume the base reduced (proof lines 14596-14597).

Identify the candidate: on a reduced scheme the coproduct of the reduced irreducible components is integral and locally birational over the base, because the components are locally finite and meet only in a controlled way (proof lines 14601-14603).

Conclude: either by the local description of the normalization through integral closures, or by the structural property that the normalization is universal for such morphisms, the normalization of the base is the coproduct of the normalizations of the components (proof lines 14598-14603).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a reduced base, then recognize the coproduct of the components of a reduced scheme as integral and locally birational and apply either the local description or the universal property of the normalization (proof lines 14596-14603).
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the normalization of a scheme with locally finitely many irreducible components as the coproduct of the normalizations of its reduced irreducible components (statement lines 14587-14594). The counted proof is short and complete: it reduces to a reduced base using that normalization is unaffected by passing to the reduction, observes that on a reduced scheme the coproduct of the components is integral and locally birational over the base, and concludes either by the local description of normalization through integral closures or by the universal property of normalization for such morphisms (proof lines 14596-14603). It is H2: the reduction and both routes to the conclusion are stated in the counted span, and the cited inputs are statements of the same chapter.
